prompts.title: Studio
prompts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: a beautiful high-fidelity desktop web app interface screenshot, landscape 16:10, sharp legible typography, polished enough to build. Single full application screen, no device frame, no browser chrome, no marketing landing-page content.
Product: "chord", an expressive live musical waveform and Lissajous instrument. The actual data visualization is the star. One note has a waveform, two notes can produce a 2D parametric curve, three notes a 3D parametric curve. This is a playful serious musical demo, no lessons, no educational prose or dashboard statistics.
Required interaction model: tabs "Waveform", "2D", "3D". Visual controls "Visual speed", "0.05×", "Freeze" (freeze graphic only). Sound has separate volume control. Instrument dropdown "Acoustic Grand Piano", "Velocity", "Sustain", computer "Keys" toggle, "Z / X octave" hint, "Connect MIDI". A real musical piano keyboard anchors the bottom; black keys in correct repeating groups of 2 and 3; compact printed shortcut labels on white keys A S D F G H J K L ; and on matching black keys W E T Y U O P. Subtle active-note colors link keyboard to plot and trace legends. Small live sound spectrum with actual thin spectral bars and octave labels, distinct from waveform traces. Labels in clear sentence case.
Constraints: intentional typography, impeccable alignment and believable implementable controls. Minimal explanatory copy, no invented marketing slogan, no lesson navigation, no giant page heading, no card grid, no ornamental widgets, no space backgrounds or random particles. The line plot must resemble a precise parametric signal trace, not a smoky nebula or a solid sculpture.
Art direction: refined dark digital studio instrument. Palette: deep ink #071421, blue slate #152B3B, cool white #EEF5FA, ice cyan #65DDE7, soft peach #FFAC8A, lavender #B49AF5. Neutral contemporary humanist sans typography with only frequency values using tabular numerals. Restrained thin rules and small 8px corner radii. Calm, precise and tactile; color belongs to the signals.
Layout: slim top bar with small lowercase chord wordmark at left, centered view tabs with 3D active, audio and Connect MIDI at right. Below, an expansive main stage occupies 74% width and about 62% screen height. Slim right sidebar about 22% width, separated by a single fine vertical line, contains three compact note rows and corresponding sine traces; then the actual live sound spectrum; then short sliders "Trail" and "Phase". At the top-left of stage small tasteful label "C major"; directly below "C3   E3   G3". 3D axes X=C3, Y=E3, Z=G3. Large centered 3D Lissajous trace of three sine signals at approximate ratio 4:5:6, drawn as dozens of exquisite fine cyan/peach/lavender lines showing nearby time trails, a complex folded wire loop with genuine depth and restrained phosphor glow. A faint perspective grid and tiny XYZ orientation marker establish camera orbit. Leave generous dark breathing space surrounding the luminous shape.
A compact transport strip directly below stage has the Freeze button, visual speed slider set to 0.05×, and small "Drag to orbit" at its right. Bottom full-width keyboard dock: instrument/velocity/sustain toolbar above a spacious realistic but understated ivory and charcoal piano spanning three octaves. C3, E3, G3 pressed with cyan, peach, lavender highlights. Very bottom concise keyboard shortcut and octave hints. Show the complete screen with no cropping. A premium audio instrument UI, an artistic plot within disciplined quiet chrome.

Art direction: striking light-mode digital gallery for sound. Cool porcelain #F7F9FC, silver blue #E2E8EF, deep marine #17375B, clear ultramarine #3159DB, rose #D26582, pale sky #B7D9EF. Soft daylight precision, matte surfaces, generous space, no beige or cream, no retro newspaper aesthetic. Clean proportional sans-serif type, bold compact lowercase wordmark, beautifully readable labels.
Layout is radically spacious and horizontal. Thin white top toolbar; small chord wordmark left, 2D active in "Waveform  2D  3D" tabs at center; Connect MIDI and volume on right. The main white plot spans nearly full width and the majority of screen height. Small note readout in upper-left "Perfect fifth", underneath two circular color swatches "C3" and "G3". Central hero is an enormous elegant deep-blue Lissajous curve, approximately x=sin(2t), y=sin(3t+0.4), one clean continuous multi-lobed trace, with a few delicately fading offset blue/rose trails to suggest slow motion. On the pale canvas, use only a very faint dotted coordinate grid and small amplitude ticks; plenty of blank space makes it spectacular. At lower-left of the canvas, two modest blue and rose time-wave traces labelled C3 and G3 are printed directly on the surface without cards. At lower-right, an equally modest spectrum with narrow blue columns and quiet octave labels. A compact pill-shaped control island below the curve contains Freeze, Visual speed 0.05×, Trail slider; it is small relative to the plot and has a subtle shadow.
Bottom 23% is an integrated light silver performance dock with instrument dropdown Acoustic Grand Piano, Velocity, Sustain, and Keys in a narrow toolbar. A full-width three-octave piano with clean white keys, deep blue-black accidentals, ultra-subtle key shadows and blue/rose C3/G3 active-note accents. Computer shortcut letters engraved delicately. Z / X octave hint and range below. This must feel like an exquisite contemporary creative tool, warm in usability but cool in color, dramatically different from a dark sci-fi interface. No marketing, no sidebar, no lesson text.

Art direction: immersive full-screen live visual instrument, cinematic but usable. Deep aubergine #180F20 and near-black plum #0D0912, parchment white #F2EAF4 for tiny text, molten coral #FF836B, electric rose #EC679F, lilac #B8A6F2. The single memorable element is an intricate luminous filament floating in enormous negative space. No neon panels, no glass cards everywhere, no stars, no cosmic imagery.
Layout: edge-to-edge plot canvas is almost the entire application background, with sparse controls placed directly over it. Small lowercase chord wordmark at top-left. View tabs at top center with 3D active; at top right tiny audio and expand icons. Plot at center is huge, finely traced and sculptural: a genuine three-frequency parametric line x=sin(4t), y=sin(5t+0.3), z=sin(6t+0.7), viewed obliquely in perspective, rendered in very thin coral-to-rose-to-lilac lines with subtle temporal trails, a complex airy folded open wireform, crisp delicate threads and slight glow at intersections. Absolutely not a thick tubular knot, sphere, smoke, or random orbital rings.
Top-left below wordmark a modest "C major" readout and three little note chips C3 E3 G3 with axis marks X Y Z. Far right, a barely-visible vertical sequence of three tiny clean orthographic projection drawings labelled XY, XZ, YZ, each about 90px; these are subordinate views of the same curve. Far left lower canvas three tiny note waveform sparklines and a compact live spectrum, directly on background, no enclosing boxes.
Near bottom center float one slim horizontal transport rail containing Freeze, a small visual speed slider, 0.05×, and "Orbit". Below it a single elegant wide shallow piano dock, about 88% viewport width, with rounded corners only at outer enclosure and very restrained depth. Slim top dock row: Acoustic Grand Piano dropdown, Velocity, Sustain, Keys, Connect MIDI, volume. Keyboard underneath full width with actual ivory and black keys, shortcut markings, and three coral/rose/lilac held keys. Footer hint Z / X octave. All controls small yet usable, no sidebar or page columns. 70% of screen is the luminous live shape and empty canvas. This is an interface you would leave running on a studio display, quiet, mature, beautiful, expressive.
